tweets.text:
I just gotta ask....why though?

Thought I'd take a look under the hood in the meantime ↓

→ Uses a real map of a fruit fly's nervous system: 166,700 neurons and roughly 25.6 million connections. The code simulates activity moving through that wiring using simplified rules.

→ Receives a small image of a Bitcoin chart. Brightness and color stimulate its visual neurons, so it's getting pixels rather than raw prices or trading indicators.

→ The developer assigns buy, sell and hold signals to specific neural activity. Activity leaning one way can mean buy; the other way can mean sell.

→ When the portfolio gains or loses value, different simulated dopamine cells get stimulated. That feedback can change some connections and potentially influence future decisions.

→ Trading limits keep it to $10 orders, 24 attempts a day and no leverage. Losing $20 stops new orders, but anything it already holds stays exposed.

This is interesting, but a fly taking trades and making money are two different things. Curious to see the results.
tweets.quoted_tweet_text:
I gave the fly brain $100 to trade bitcoin.

Dopamine neurons are stimulated when the fly makes profit. Neuron activity controls buy/sell decisions and makes trades on coinbase.

Will the fly get rich? https://t.co/XVWSFattGu

• below parity → issuance pauses

UPDATED: My current top picks 👇
September 13, 2026

My top-picks list is back, and several of these companies are approaching milestones that could change their story. Here’s what’s changed since the last update, where my conviction stands, and what I’m watching next.

☢️ URANIUM

Producers & Developers

$CCJ – My blue-chip uranium pick. Westinghouse has confidentially filed for a potential IPO, adding another development to watch alongside Cameco’s uranium business. Exposure across the nuclear fuel and reactor supply chain remains the appeal.

$KAP – Moody’s affirmed its Baa1 rating and upgraded its standalone credit assessment to baa2 on September 9. I still like the scale and cost position, with production execution and input costs worth watching closely.

$DNN – Phoenix construction remains the central catalyst. The latest report showed key first-year milestones on track, while uranium inventory sales generated funding without issuing new shares. Execution is now what matters most.

$NXE – Rook I is under construction, moving this enormous uranium project into its next phase. The resource scale remains exceptional; financing, construction costs and delivery are the milestones I’m watching.

$UUUU – Completed the Australian Strategic Materials acquisition on August 28, adding operating rare-earth metal and alloy capabilities in South Korea. A significant step toward an integrated Western supply chain, alongside its uranium exposure.

$UEC – Burke Hollow and its Wyoming operations underpin the U.S. production growth story. Unhedged uranium exposure remains the attraction; the next test is translating the expanded operating footprint into higher production.

Explorers

$SYH – Filed independent NI 43-101 technical reports for Moore and Russell Lake on September 3. Still one of my preferred Athabasca prospect generators, combining flagship exploration with multiple partner-funded programs.

$M.CN – All three initial Gem holes hit broad, shallow uranium mineralization, including 34.9 m at 210 ppm eU₃O₈ from 10.65 m. Encouraging expansion beyond Lucky Cliff, although these are preliminary radiometric estimates pending laboratory assays.

🥈 SILVER

Producers

$HL – The latest quarter delivered 4.2M oz of silver, including record production at Lucky Friday. Operational delivery remains the reason it stays among my preferred silver producers.

$AG – September 9 drilling results highlighted high-grade mineralization and an expanding exploration footprint at San Dimas. Resource conversion and additions provide another catalyst alongside its producing operations.

$PAAS – Q2 delivered 6.47M oz of attributable silver production and $344M in attributable free cash flow, with annual operating guidance reaffirmed. Cash generation and La Colorada Skarn remain the key attractions.

Explorers & Developers

$HYMC – Fresh September drilling returned 30.5 m at 780.53 g/t silver at Vortex. Continued expansion of its high-grade systems keeps the exploration story compelling, with metallurgy and development economics still crucial.

$GRSL.V – September 8 drilling extended mineralization at San Marcial, including 16.1 m at 162 g/t silver and 11.7 m at 147 g/t. Further resource growth remains the main attraction.

$JTWO – My wildcard. Sierra Plata mapping identified seven veins, with channel sampling returning 811 g/t silver over 1.4 m. Encouraging early evidence as the company prepares drill targets and permitting; these are sampling results, not drill intersections.

🟠 COPPER

$CGNT.V – My primary copper exposure. Fresh Mocoa drilling returned 771 m at 0.54% CuEq, followed by an OTCQX upgrade in September. The scale of the system and continued drilling remain the core reasons I’m following it.

⚫ GRAPHENE

$HG $HGRAF – Still my largest holding. HydroGraph completed an upsized C$70.4M financing in August, strengthening its funding position. Texas scale-up and converting customer development work into commercial orders remain the catalysts I’m watching most closely.

📊 YTD share price performance for all 16 companies in the attached table.

Disclosure: I have paid partnerships with Myriad Uranium and Skyharbour Resources.

Not financial advice. Please do your own due diligence.

tweets.text:
#uranium #silver #copper #gold

⚡ DAILY METALS PULSE — SEPTEMBER 13 ⚡

Four metals. One pulse. No noise.

The macro picture is getting wild.

Oil >$100.
US 10Y flirting with 5%.
Inflation sticky.
Fed hike odds ~85%.
Middle East supply routes under pressure.
Yet commodities refuse to roll over.

☢️ URANIUM
This may be the most important uranium quote of the week:
Kazatomprom says it could easily sell ALL of its uranium production “into the East.���

Think about that.

Western utilities still need to contract huge future requirements while China, India and other Eastern buyers are becoming increasingly aggressive.

Spot is around $90/lb and long-term prices are at multi-year highs.

This increasingly looks less like another uranium cycle...

and more like a global competition for secure nuclear fuel.

⚡ COPPER
Copper is knocking on $15,000/t.

LME recently traded around $14,700+ after hitting fresh records.

Mine production fell 1.1% in H1 while concentrate output dropped 2.6%.

Meanwhile AI, grids, electrification and data centers keep demanding more metal.

And inventories are geographically distorted as huge quantities of copper have been pulled toward the US.

High prices are supposed to cure high prices.

But you can't build a copper mine overnight.

🥈 SILVER
Silver finished around $64.50 after bouncing strongly Friday.

The physical thesis hasn't changed:

Sixth consecutive market deficit expected.
Mine supply basically stagnant.
Physical investment recovering.
India potentially returning as a major buyer.

Solar thrifting is the main bearish fundamental — but AI, electronics, grids and automotive demand are growing.

And despite an increasingly hawkish Fed, buyers stepped in again Friday.

Silver doesn't need every demand category to boom.

It needs investment demand to collide with a market already running structural deficits.

🥇 GOLD
Gold bounced back above $4,350 Friday despite CPI pushing Fed hike odds toward 85%.

That's interesting.

Normally:

Higher inflation → higher yields → stronger Fed expectations → weaker gold.

Yet buyers appeared quickly.

Why?

Because the alternative isn't particularly attractive either.

Oil above $100 is feeding inflation.
Government deficits remain enormous.
Bond yields are approaching dangerous territory.
Geopolitical risk keeps rising.

Central banks and investors increasingly face the same question:

Where do you hide purchasing power?

Gold keeps providing the answer.

🔥 THE BIG PICTURE

This is the setup I keep coming back to:

Mining costs ↑
Energy costs ↑
Financing costs ↑
Permitting times ↑
Ore grades ↓

Short-term volatility? Absolutely.

But the cure for high commodity prices is new supply.

And new supply is becoming harder and MORE EXPENSIVE to build.

That is why I'm staying bullish on my four metals.

tweets.text:
Amodei, Altman and Musk agree they need to pace the frontier ie *slow* the rate of new capability so safety can catch up. This is not a halt.

Two drivers they cite: faster recursive self-improvement and agent breakouts (Hugging Face etc.). 

Plan: embedded third-party evaluators (Anthropic now, OpenAI says it will follow), lab coordination and don’t gift the lead to China.

Motive: Is this being done for safety or as a competitive moat? Probably both. Closed labs can absorb auditors, regulatory oversight costs and gates. Open weights can’t recall a model once it’s out. Amodei says rules should hit the frontier harder than challengers. Skeptics say the opposite happens in practice.

Markets: Monday may see a knee-jerk reaction in chips and AI-stocks. That’s sentiment.

Thesis: largely unchanged. Pacing peak models ≠ stopping inference, AI agents or data centres. Demand is still tokens, power and clusters. 

We’ll change our view if capex and GPU orders actually roll over - not because of a blogpost on the weekend. 
https://t.co/YKr5pL7G2c
